law_name: Statut du bailleur prive ('dispositif Jeanbrun'), enacted via the Finance Act for 2026 (loi n. 2026-103 du 19 fevrier 2026)
description: A private-landlord status creating a new rental-investment incentive. Landlords can deduct an annual fiscal amortisation of 3.5% to 5.5% of 80% of a qualifying property's acquisition value from rental income, generating a deductible property deficit (deficit foncier) capped at 10,700 EUR/year for new-build and 21,400 EUR for substantially renovated properties, in exchange for capped rents under intermediate, social or very-social commitments, with a minimum nine-year rental commitment in tension zones A bis, A, B1 and B2. In force 21 February 2026 to 31 December 2028.
significance: Jeanbrun's principal legislative achievement as minister, intended as the successor to the expired Pinel scheme and designed to generate roughly 50,000 additional housing units per year. The measure drew criticism from some architects and urban planners who feared it could compromise construction-quality standards.
